topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Well, now, it seems the oak by the old mill has been taken down. I remember when little Jimmy planted that acorn, barely taller than a stalk of wheat himself. It’s a sight to see how fast the years run, faster than the stream after spring thaw. That oak grew strong, sheltered many a lamb and gave shade to more than one lad resting from his labor. I wager the wood will find good use, but the field feels less with it gone. Aye, the world moves on, and with it, the things we hold dear.
